decision: ADR-020 §3 (scheduler decision 2026-10-09): Action definitions NexLoop itself needs are published at deployment through trusted configuration (0050), compiled from this versioned declaration; never constructed ad hoc and never written to definition tables directly. Human-owner Actions (authority human_owner) are granted to the owner's human principal, never to service principals. v4 (dispatcher ruling 2026-10-10, NX-050): the service ontology.object.edit Capability profile, declared through Consumer.edit:1 (executed by claim_matcher, whose grant is already in service-grants). Review-approved new types reuse the tenant's published ontology.object.create / ontology.object.edit snapshots for their <Type>.create / <Type>.edit (0101); a capability definition, not a grant.

actions.purpose: Governed formal Consumer property write of an accepted Claim match (NX-020); also publishes the tenant's ontology.object.edit Capability snapshot that review-approved new types reuse for <Type>.edit (NX-044/NX-050). Object and property EDIT are still decided per object.
Create the Message object of an Agent reply after the channel accepted it (NX-047); content, sender, conversation and delivery state come from the governed outbound record, never from the caller.
Publish the next immutable version of a Context strategy (budgets, quotas, trim order). Human owner only; SQL refuses services and Agents even with a grant (NX-023).

Read one model-call Manifest (sources, versions, request digest). Humans only (owner / audit role, owner decision 2026-10-09); SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant; never in service-grants (NX-023).
